items.title: 68437_Charles Thompson oral history interview
items.q: Billie Holliday was always a pleasure to play with

ctx.x: I was always a guy that liked to play jazz. We wanted to play jazz. And we didn't mind playing for singers, really, who we thought were good. Like Billie Holliday was always a pleasure to play with, if she was feeling well, and, you know -- but you know, it just was a thing you did as a chore.

items.title: 68437_Charles Thompson oral history interview
items.q: Joe Guy was their trumpet player who later married Billie Holiday, you know about him.

ctx.x: Who was in that band, can you remember?
Oh, there's plenty guys. Joe Guy was their trumpet player who later married Billie Holiday, you know about him. Oh, a lot of musicians played them. I could name quite a few of them.

items.title: 68437_Charles Thompson oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] He named Billie Lady Day and he named you Sir Charles.

ctx.x: In fact I would have to say, with all sincerity, Lester Young loved me as a piano player, as a musician, as a guy. As I said because I met him earlier in Omaha, Nebraska when I first started, he knew me from the beginning and he knew my interest in music, and he knew I was really serious about music, and that I liked his music, and his style, and I liked him. And he was just beautiful.
He named Billie Lady Day and he named you Sir Charles.

Yes, he was quite capable -- he always was naming people. In fact the way I got the name, when I got to New York they were playing in the famous Cafe Society, which was the most high class jazz night club in the world as has ever been. And of course later on Billy Berg had one too in Hollywood, and I came there with Coleman Hawkins later.
